system: mixed system of French civil law and customary law

constitution.history: several previous; latest approved by referendum 25 October 2015
constitution.amend: proposed by the president of the republic or by Parliament; passage of presidential proposals requires Supreme Court review followed by approval in a referendum; such proposals may also be submitted directly to Parliament, in which case passage requires at least three-quarters majority vote of both houses in joint session; proposals by Parliament require three-fourths majority vote of both houses in joint session; constitutional articles including those affecting the country's territory, republican form of government, and secularity of the state are not amendable

courts.highest: Supreme Court or Cour Supreme (consists of NA judges); Constitutional Court (consists of 9 members)
courts.judges: Supreme Court judges elected by Parliament and serve until age 65; Constitutional Court members appointed by the president of the republic - 3 directly by the president and 6 nominated by Parliament; members appointed for renewable 9-year terms with one third of the membership renewed every 3 years
courts.lower: Court of Audit and Budgetary Discipline; courts of appeal; regional and district courts; employment tribunals; juvenile courts
courts.note: a High Court of Justice, outside the judicial authority, tries cases involving treason by the President of the Republic

citizenship.descent: at least one parent must be a citizen of the Republic of the Congo

world: has not submitted an ICJ jurisdiction declaration; accepts ICCt jurisdiction
